title: Ginat Egoz (Hebrew, 1615 imprint)
author: Joseph Gikatilla
description: Ginat Egoz (The Garden of Nuts) by Joseph Gikatilla, here in a Hebrew printed edition (the index gives 1615; the first printing was Hanau, 1614-15). Written in 1274 when Gikatilla was in his twenties and under the influence of Abraham Abulafia, it belongs to his early, more philosophical and linguistic phase, before Sha'arei Orah. Its title alludes to the Song of Songs (6:11) and to the nut as a symbol of the hidden kernel of mystical wisdom within its shells. It has three parts: on the divine names and the mysteries of the Tetragrammaton; on the letters of the Hebrew alphabet and their combinations, gematria and permutations (techniques related to Abulafia's prophetic Kabbalah); and on the vowel points and their mystical significance. It provides a bridge between philosophical and Kabbalistic understandings of language as the instrument of creation.
